chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of marrying the Zanj, for he is a creation that is deformed.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الزِّنْجِ: The Zanj (a specific ethnic group, often associated with East Africans)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying Zanj people according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) advises avoiding marriage with the Zanj, describing them as 'deformed creation' (kalq mushawwah). While often interpreted as a reference to physical characteristics or distinct racial traits in the historical context of early Islam, Shia scholars also view it as a specific ruling (hukm) regarding social compatibility rather than a universal prohibition on all Zanj individuals. This narration is frequently discussed in the context of *kafa'ah* (marital equality) and the criteria for selecting spouses within Shia jurisprudence.
